Subject: Recap + next steps: deployment mode & compliance (HIPAA / SOC2 / BAA)

Hi Carlos / Janelle 

Thanks again for the call today  good to meet you both. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary (from our discovery)
- Primary use: PHI-enabled clinical note summarization and triage for Acme's care coordination product.
- Volume: ~500k tokens/day initially, expected to double over 12 months.
- Latency target: P95 < 500ms for chat endpoints.
- Compliance: HIPAA covered; must sign a BAA. Security team requires SOC 2 Type II evidence and architecture diagrams for data flows.
- Deployment preference: security team asked us to surface the options (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC/on-prem) and pros/cons for each given HIPAA + audit requirements.

Attachments I'm sharing with this note: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf, BAA_template_Redwood.docx, deployment_modes_onepager.pdf.

Open questions / asks for Acme:
1) Please confirm the primary security contact (Janelle listed on the call; please confirm email).
2) Can you confirm whether Acme requires customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production PHI? If yes, that makes Private VPC or on-prem more likely.
3) Any special audit window / evidence needs (e.g., SOC report review onsite, penetration test reports)?

Proposed next steps
- I'll loop in Rishi (solutions) to outline how each deployment mode satisfies HIPAA/BAA and what additional evidence we can provide.
- Provide a mutual action plan and timelines for procurement and security review (I attached a MAP template).
- Schedule a 30-45 min tech deep-dive with your security/infra folks  are mornings this week available?

If helpful, here's a short summary upfront: 
- Hosted API: fastest to start, Redwood will process requests in our shared hosted environment; HIPAA support via BAA + strict access controls, but no customer-managed KMS. Best if you're comfortable with vendor-managed keys and need fast time-to-value.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools for Acme only (logical isolation), predictable throughput, supports some customer keying options and stricter network controls; often a middle ground for enterprises balancing time-to-value and control.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full network isolation, customer-managed keys, and air-gapped options for regulated deployments. Longer lead time and higher ops overhead.

Thanks  I'll wait for Janelle to confirm security contact and for Carlos to confirm key management preference.

Marissa

Hi Carlos / Janelle 

Thanks for the notes  happy to run the tech deep-dive. A few clarifications to prepare the session and the architecture docs you requested: 

Data flow & storage
- Redwood's runtime processes requests in-memory and uses a KV cache for model context; we do not persist inbound request payloads to long-term storage by default.
- For Hosted API, logs and telemetry are stored in vendor managed systems (can be provided as audit extracts). No customer-managed KMS in shared hosted.
- For Dedicated, we can provide network isolation and options to integrate with your cloud KMS for envelope encryption on persisted artifacts and model caching layers.
- Private VPC / On-prem: full control over keys and networking; you can choose to run the inference runtime within your VPC or on-prem hardware.

Audit evidence
- SOC2 Type II report (attached) covers controls across security/availability/confidentiality for our hosting environment. We can provide a redacted penetration test summary; full reports are provided under NDA if required.
- For BAAs, we use the attached BAA template which most customers sign with minor redlines.

Prep ask for the call
1) Please share high-level architecture of where Acme's PHI originates (EHR? ingestion pipeline?), what systems will call Redwood, and whether Acme requires on-host encryption for KV cache.
2) Janelle: confirm whether Acme requires remote SOC 2 review or in-person audits.

I'm attaching a short deployment_modes_onepager.pdf that summarizes the three modes and the security/evidence we can provide per mode. Happy to schedule 45 min for a technical walkthrough  I’m available Fri 16th 09:00-11:00 PT or Mon 19th 10:00-13:00 PT.

Thanks  Rishi
